Applicant :- Gopi Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Rai,Swatantra Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Pradeep Kumar Rai, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri J.B. Singh, learned Aga
for the State.
2.

This is an application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of complaint and its summoning order dated 14.03.2023 as well as order dated 08.08.2024 by which issued Non Bailable Warrant against the applicant in Complaint Case No.101 of 2022 (Ayushi Vs.
Gopi Singh and others), under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Kalpi,
District Jalaun, pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jalaun at Orai.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that a complaint was lodged by the opposite party no.2 on 10.08.2021 against the applicant herein along with others, under 156(3) Cr.P.C. with relation to commission of the offences under Sections 376, 342, 323, 504, 506 IPC with an allegation that post death of the mother of the opposite party no.2her father married another woman, however,
they were not showering affection pursuant whereto the opposite party no.2 was living with applicant.

sentences.text: Allegation is that applicant committed bad acts and outraged the modesty of the opposite party no.2 and she was also not taken care of.
The complaint was lodged on 03.08.2021 before the Superintendent of Police followed by the proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
Statements under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. were recorded and, thereafter, the applicant has been summoned under the aforesaid penal sections.
Questioning the summoning order applicant has filed the present application.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for a single moment, particularly, in view of the fact there happens to be a police report which is annexure no.4 at page 58 of the paper book.

On on objection taken by the applicant that opposite party no.2 had fell in love with a boy and it was neither right age nor there was any reason to do so that became a matter of anguish and the opposite party no.2 just in order to settle this core proceeded to lodge the proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., wherein, serious allegations have been levelled.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that even the opposite party no.2 was not subjected to medical examination and in case, medical examination was done the truth would have surfaced.
He further submits that police report has not been taken into consideration while summoning the applicant also.
7. Learned AGA, on the other hand, submits that whatever might be the present case may not be a case, wherein, interference is warranted, particularly, when the allegations are serious.
8. I have heard submission so made across the bar and perused the records carefully.
9. Apparently, a complaint is stated to have been lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicant and the other co-accused regarding outraging the modesty and committing the bad acts.

As regards the submission so sought to be raised by the learned counsel for the applicant that there happens to be a police report and the existence of the same would completely overruled, the possibility even in remotest case of commission of the offence is concerned, this Court is not require to dwell into this issue and what would be relevant at the stage of summoning in a complaint case would be the allegations in the complaint and the statement under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.
10.
The import and the effect of the police report is to be decided on its own strength when the trail commences and when a decision is to be taken whether the accused is to be convicted or acquitted.

Nonetheless, non subjection of medical examination of the victim would not be fatal, particularly,
when the same is also a subject matter whose effect and ramifications are to be adjudged when the trial commences and final decision is to be taken for acquittal or conviction.
11.
Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case bearing in mind that there are no material contradictions in the statements viz-a-viz the complaint, hence, no case is made out for interference.
12. Accordingly, application is rejected and consigned to records.
